source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 20 September 1946, p. 3 ("Nominations for county and rural councils")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: Read on the page image: the News-Letter's Castlereagh section lists each division with its nominee (no party labels printed; the recorded party is not from this page). The Northern Whig's list of the same day (p. 3), cited before, does not carry this council.

note: Triennial election, polled Thursday 3 October 1946. Only five nominations were received for the nine seats; three divisions had no candidates and their sitting members were deemed re-elected, while Ballycultra was left to a casual vacancy. Ballycultra was left to a casual vacancy after the sitting member was found ineligible. Ballycultra was filled by the council as a casual vacancy: William Albert Ryan, the only nominee, was appointed (Belfast Telegraph, 31 October 1946, p. 6). A co-option, not an election (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Citation corrected (w19-bna-fix, Nov 2026): the Northern Whig page cited before (20 September 1946, p. 3) has no Castlereagh list; the member is named in the Belfast News-Letter of the same day, p. 3 (page image), which prints no party labels, so Party_As_Printed is cleared (the recorded party is kept). Party (w19-fixes2, 19 Nov 2026): the recorded UUP had no source, since the Belfast News-Letter list of 20 September 1946, p. 3 prints no party labels. No party is recorded (unknown), as there is no consistent evidence: his return before (Alexander Robb 1939) carries no label.
